messages:
maria_support: FYI customer hitting a 400 on a tool call to `pdf_gen`. They pasted their payload and curl. says it worked yesterday. stack:

maria_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\n    "tool": "pdf_gen",\n    "args": {\n      "title": "Q2 Campaign",\n      "file_path": "C:\\Users\\Marketing\\campaign.json",\n    }\n  }'```

maria_support: Error returned: `400 malformed_tool_args - invalid JSON payload (Unexpected token \" at position 92)` — customer says they didn't change client.

josh_cs: Can you get the call_id and SDK/platform version? Also which region?

maria_support: call_id=rc-20240625-9b2f, region=us-west1, client=customer-node-1.2.3. They attached our server log: `parse_error: invalid escape sequence`

emily_devex: Likely escaping issue with the Windows path backslashes and the trailing comma after `file_path`. Two quick repros: 1) curl exactly as pasted should reproduce; 2) node `fetch` example below (customer often sends nested JSON as string).

emily_devex: ```js
// bad (stringified inner JSON + backslashes)
await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-REDACTED', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    tool: 'pdf_gen',
    args: JSON.stringify({ title: 'Q2 Campaign', file_path: 'C:\\Users\\Marketing\\campaign.json', }),
  }),
});
```

emily_devex: That ends up double-encoding the inner object and leaves backslashes that need escaping. Also trailing commas are invalid JSON (some clients allow them but our parser is strict).

liang_eng: Checked the trace for rc-20240625-9b2f — parser fails before schema validation. Raw body we received (sanitized) shows the inner `args` value arrived as a string starting with `"{\"title\":\"Q2 Campaign\",\"file_path\":\"C:\\\\Users\\\\Marketing\\\\campaign.json\",}"` — so double-encoded + trailing comma. Our JSON parser throws at the extra comma after the path.

liang_eng: Quick mitigation: ask client to send `args` as an object (not a JSON string) and remove trailing commas. If they're using the SDK, ensure they pass a JS object, not `JSON.stringify(args)`. Also ensure Content-Type is `application/json` (not form-encoded).

maria_support: Passed suggested repro & fix to customer. They tried `body: JSON.stringify({ tool: 'pdf_gen', args: { title: 'Q2 Campaign', file_path: 'C:\\Users\\Marketing\\campaign.json' } })` and still hit error. They pasted new error: `invalid escape sequence in string`

emily_devex: Hmm — that usually means the client source file itself had unescaped backslashes before serialization (rare). Ask them to try forward slashes or double-escape: `C:\\Users\\Marketing\\campaign.json` in the JS literal (but they shouldn't have to if they use normal strings). Also confirm they're running the same Node version.

maria_support: Customer tried `file_path: 'C:/Users/Marketing/campaign.json'` and it succeeded 👍

redwood-deploy-bot: Detected related parser update 2024-05-10 on runtime that removed tolerant trailing-comma parsing. If you need a soft-fail for a specific org, we can enable legacy-tolerant-json for a short window but requires eng approval.

liang_eng: We should not enable org-wide tolerant mode by default. Customer docs already mention strict JSON. I'll leave a note in the ticket explaining the change and the exact repro + suggested client fixes (use forward slashes or double-escape in source, avoid trailing commas, don't stringify inner args).

maria_support: I'll send the final message and mark as `awaiting customer` — thanks. :white_check_mark:
